statements.t: This information is intended to facilitate the understanding and assessment of significant changes and trends related to the Company’s results of operations and financial condition.
We expect our relationship-focused business model to continue generating organic growth from existing customers and to expand our targeted customer bases.

The Company actively monitors construction and land loan exposures through underwriting standards, project-specific reviews, and ongoing oversight of borrower performance, project progress, and collateral values.
The allowance for credit losses represents management’s estimate of expected credit losses of financial assets measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet credit exposures.
Liquidity risk is the risk that the Company will be unable to meet its obligations as they come due without incurring unacceptable losses or significantly increasing funding costs.
The Company’s liquidity management framework is designed to maintain sufficient liquidity to meet expected and unexpected cash flow obligations under both normal and stressed market conditions.
The Company does not expect these commitments as of September 30, 2026 to have a material current or future impact on the Company’s liquidity, financial condition or results of operations.
Management believes that East West has sufficient liquidity to meet the projected cash obligations for at least the next 12 months.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company believes it has maintained sufficient liquidity resources to support ongoing operations, meet contractual obligations, and satisfy expected and potential contingent funding requirements under both normal and stressed operating conditions.

The simulation does not represent a forecast of the Company’s net interest income but is a tool utilized to assess the risk of the impact of changing market interest rates across a range of interest rate environments.
The Company uses these deposit repricing models to forecast deposit interest expense.

As loan and debt security prepayment assumptions are key components of the Company’s model, the Company incorporates third-party vendor models to forecast prepayment behavior on mortgage loans and securities, which have mortgage loans as underlying collateral.
The Company actively manages deposit pricing and employs quantitative models to evaluate and forecast deposit behavior under various interest rate scenarios.
This long-term economic perspective into the Company’s interest rate risk profile allows the Company to identify anticipated negative effects of interest rate fluctuations.
As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s EVE is expected to decrease when interest rates rise.
